candidates.detail: The public FitBody/Realization inputs carry packed joint ordinals and separate f32 weights. GpuBody::new checks nonzero vertex count, row lengths, rig bounds and face indices but not whether any weights support the chosen anatomical region. If named landmarks exist, buffers are accepted and a selected limb fit is successfully recorded and submitted with all-zero weights, the support shader gives every vertex zero support. If a station invocation reaches the selection and hull code with those zero support values, it selects no points, leaves unique and hull at zero, and decrements the u32 hull once per each of two halves. Earlier shader arithmetic and backend behavior are not established. Under the cited WGSL concrete-integer arithmetic rule this yields 4,294,967,294, which becomes the bound of the subsequent center-accumulation loop. If the invocation continues far enough, its sample reads leave the allocated station-sample buffer; the standard permits multiple dynamic-error outcomes. No body, device, shader, GPU loop, or out-of-bounds access was executed.
candidates.consumer_and_safeguards: The selected limb path records a frame, part and clearance kernels into the same batch. Frame generation can mark NoEnvelope when no weighted skin bounds exist, but this status is staged and checked only after batch submission and device readback; it does not by itself show that the clearance station dispatch was suppressed. If a completed readback reports the frame failure, the host returns an error before assembling a successful part. Actual GPU completion, shader dynamic-error handling, a generated MHR body with this support state, and a player-visible failure are not established. The public inputs require valid rig ordinals and names; the constructed zero-weight state is a source-level conditional, not a proven ordinary asset.
candidates.connected_scope: Packed skin ordinals and weight admission, fit body/realization and selected limb producer, frame and clearance dispatch ordering, station minimum/degeneracy and status propagation, readback and all downstream GPU consumers.
candidates.proposed_repair: After complete discovery and implementation authorization, ensure empty or insufficient unique planar support fails with a bounded status before hull decrement, section writes and downstream use, or prove and enforce a stronger admission invariant at the true owner. Propagate failure through the existing part/frame status while preserving valid low-sample behavior where intentional.
candidates.later_acceptance: When product validation is authorized, cover no support, a single unique point, degenerate and normal multi-point sections, status ordering and selected limb/mitten paths on supported device backends; establish bounded work and a recoverable error without relying on a later frame readback to prevent earlier execution.
